findings: Solved 2026-10-29 on the owner's request (Practice, Book exercises): the Chapter 17 exercise as printed (PDF 115-117, printed 111-113) with answers in English and Roman Urdu: 10 MCQs, 7 short answer, 7 constructed response, 6 comprehensive questions and 6 numerical problems. Drafts for the academic review.
The book prints no MCQ key; the keys are worked out from the chapter: 1 a, 2 b, 3 c, 4 d, 5 a, 6 b, 7 c, 8 d, 9 a, 10 b.

Owner rule BOOK-CORRECTION-01 applied: all printed questions and options keep the book's wording; checkpoints carry no book_errors field, so each wrong item is explained in a Book correction / Kitab ki ghalti box after the question.

MCQ 3: no option is correct. The RC-time constant is RC = 10 kOhm x 0.05 uF = 0.5 ms; option (c) 0.549 ms = RC ln 3 (time to charge to 2/3 of 36 V). (c) is keyed as the intended answer with a Book correction box.

MCQ 6: the circuit is said to be at resonance, but the printed reactances are unequal (120 and 150 Ohm). The intended working (Z = R = 24 Ohm, V_L = 220/24 x 120 = 1100 V) gives (b) 1.1 kV; with the reactances as given V_L = 687 V (no option). Option (b) prints the unit 'KV' (kV). Explained in a Book correction box.
MCQ 2 option (d) prints '0.0415 Ma' (unit mA); MCQ 9 prints '4 time' (4 times). Both kept as printed and noted in Book correction boxes.
Comprehensive 17.1 and 17.2 print 'is an AC circuit' for 'in an AC circuit'; kept as printed, noted in Book correction boxes.
Book correction, numerical 17.3: printed 3000 V; with M = 1.5 H and the current rising 0 to 1 A in T/4 = 0.005 s, the mean emf is 300 V (= 0.637 x peak emf M w Io = 471 V). 3000 V would need 500 Hz.

Numerical 17.4 prints 'the reactance X_L of capacitor' (should be X_C); kept as printed with a Book correction box. Its printed 27.63 A differs from 220/7.958 = 27.65 A (220/7.96 = 27.64 A) only by rounding.

Numerical 17.1: 'configure' and 'current in the circuits' kept as printed (noted in a box). Part (b) uses the series RC impedance (Z = 82.05 Ohm, I = 1.34 A as printed); the printed answer (c), current leads by 90 degrees, is the phase for the capacitor; for the whole RC circuit the lead is 75.9 degrees (given in both languages).
Numericals 17.1, 17.2, 17.4 (apart from rounding), 17.5 and 17.6 agree with the printed answers.
Minor print slips kept without boxes: CRQ 17.7 'is fatal what causes death' (run-on), MCQ 17.6 option (a) '1030  V' (extra space, transcribed '1030 V'), numerical 17.6 'an resistance'.

Comprehensive 17.3 gives Q = R sqrt(C/L) for the parallel circuit (Q rises with R); the chapter text (17.13) says Q is inversely proportional to R, which its lesson already corrects; the Roman Urdu has a Wazahat box. Comprehensive 17.6 states that VI cos theta is the true power and VI the apparent power (the chapter's 17.12 wording calls VI cos theta apparent power, corrected in its lesson). Comprehensive 17.5 describes the bridge circuit and the input/output waveforms in words (no figures added); 'signal phasor diagrams' is read as the input and output waveforms.

Beyond the chapter (labelled in the answers): short 17.1 and 17.4 (RC time constant, charging to 63%), short 17.2 (AC line touching a DC line), CRQ 17.3 (safety measures, mostly), CRQ 17.7 (the term ventricular fibrillation). MCQs 3 and 8 also rely on the time constant RC, which the chapter does not define.
